title: BIS Quarterly Review, December 2025
summary: The BIS Quarterly Review December 2025 features extensive coverage of global FX and interest rate derivatives market structure, including highlights from the 2025 Triennial Survey and detailed analysis of the cash-futures basis trade and post-Libor interest rate derivatives markets.
key_points: 2025 BIS Triennial Survey provides new data on global FX market turnover and hedging activity
FX volumes surged in April 2025 amid tariff news, with hedging taking center stage in trading behavior
Cash-futures basis trade and exchange-traded interest rate derivatives positioning examined in detail
Post-Libor benchmark reform has structurally shifted OTC interest rate derivatives markets
Euro contracts have migrated to Germany following benchmark reform
Renminbi growth is propelling EME currency trading expansion
Concentration of clearing in OTC IRD markets poses challenges for emerging market economies

The 2025 Triennial Survey data is essential for anyone analyzing FX market depth and mechanics. The analysis of the cash-futures basis trade and post-Libor market structure directly affects how hedge funds, dealers, and institutional participants operate.
macro_context: The December 2025 edition covers market reactions to policy tightening and tariff-related volatility, providing context for how derivatives markets absorbed macro shocks in 2025.
market_structure_context: Core focus: global FX and derivatives market structure including Triennial Survey data, cash-futures basis dynamics, OTC-to-exchange migration post-Libor, clearing concentration risks, and EME derivatives market development.
